title: Quantized op canonicalization + concurrency regression: follow-up & remediation
creator: Avery Li
description: Summary: A production incident on 2026-03-09 exposed an interaction between the quantized operator canonicalizer and our concurrent batch scheduler that produced two failure modes: 1) intermittent OOMs/crash loops for low-batch (<4) streaming requests on certain LLMs using int4 kernels, and 2) subtle per-token distribution shifts (accuracy drift) when the canonicalizer reordered fused-attention ops under concurrent execution. This ticket consolidates findings, decisions, and concrete action items to prevent recurrence and restore confidence in quantized rollouts.
impact: Affected ~2% of hosted model traffic for two model families (redwood/ora-1, open/fastgpt-6B-quant). Errors manifested as task restarts and elevated decoding perplexity for a subset of prompts. Several enterprise customers reported degraded output quality leading to rollback of quantized build on Dedicated pools.

root_cause: A non-deterministic canonicalization rewrite in the quantization-aware optimizer reorders fused attention microkernels in a way that is safe in float32 but changes the write/read interleaving of the KV cache in int4 execution. Under concurrency (continuous batching and streaming), the altered ordering produced stale/overwritten cache entries and amplified dequant rounding noise, causing OOMs in low-batch flows and measurable distribution shifts in generation for specific prompt patterns.
mitigation: Hotfix: Disable the canonicalizer optimization for int4 quantized kernels on all production pools until deterministic variant lands (done: 2026-03-09)
Canary: Expand canary tests to include low-batch streaming mixes and long-tail sequence prompt set used by reported customers
Emergency config: Add a temporary throttle that forces batch size >= 4 on affected nodepools to avoid low-batch OOM trigger (applied to Dedicated customers impacted)
Telemetry: Add op-level deterministic hashes and KV-cache version tagging to trace and detect reorder-induced mismatches

decisions: Do not ship canonicalizer for int4 until deterministic semantics and KV-cache ordering invariants are proven by tests and canary coverage
Prefer deterministic transforms over heuristic reorders when they interact with stateful components like KV-cache
Adopt a canary policy that includes both low-batch streaming and concurrent fanout scenarios for any quantization-related runtime change
notes: During triage we observed two orthogonal failure modes; treating them as linked prevented parallel workstreams from talking past each other.
Contributors: Diego Morales, Rina Patel, Marco Chen, Priya Singh (Evaluations), SRE on-call (Jordan Blake)
Follow-up will include an RFC for invariants that any optimizer pass must preserve when interacting with mutable runtime state
